title: Power-Law Relaxation of Non-Gaussian Parameter and Self-Dynamic Structure Factor in Multidimensional Rugged Energy Landscapes
abstract: Ruggedness of the underlying energy landscape gives rise to heterogeneous mobility and non-Gaussian diffusion. We develop a theoretical framework for tagged-particle diffusion in multidimensional rugged energy landscapes modeled as correlated quenched Gaussian random fields. Using the self-propagator and self-dynamic structure factor, we characterize finite-time diffusion beyond the effective diffusion coefficient. We determine the effects of dimensionality, spatial correlations, and initial preparation. By introducing a coarse-grained mobility field and a mobility-memory approximation, we relate the non-Gaussian parameter to the time correlation of the mobility sampled by the particle. In the homogenized diffusive regime, the mobility correlation decays algebraically, leading to long-time relaxation of the non-Gaussian parameter as $t^{-1/2}$ in one dimension, $(\ln t)/t$ in two dimensions, and $t^{-1}$ for $d>2$, with amplitudes that depend on dimensionality and the initial ensemble. Our results show that rugged energy landscapes leave distinct signatures in the effective diffusion coefficient, self-dynamic structure factor, and relaxation of non-Gaussian fluctuations.
summary: This theoretical work develops a rigorous framework to study diffusion on rugged energy landscapes by analyzing the time evolution of higher moments, particularly the non-Gaussian parameter. It establishes that this relaxation exhibits distinct power-law scaling depending on dimensionality ($d$), providing a sensitive diagnostic tool beyond simple effective diffusion coefficients.
main_problem: The research aims to characterize finite-time diffusion dynamics, specifically focusing on the power-law relaxation of non-Gaussian parameters ($\alpha_2(t)$) and the self-dynamic structure factor in multidimensional rugged energy landscapes.
main_result: The paper predicts dimension-dependent power-law decays for $\alpha_2(t)$: $t^{-1/2}$ in 1D, $(\ln t)/t$ in 2D, and $t^{-1}$ for $d>2$, which serve as distinct signatures of mobility heterogeneity.
method: The theoretical framework uses a propagator-based approach derived from the master equation, relating higher moments (like $\alpha_2(t)$) to the time correlation of the local diffusivity field via a mobility-memory approximation.
model_or_system: The system is tagged-particle diffusion on a multidimensional lattice with quenched disorder, where hopping rates are governed by site energies following the Miller–Abrahams rule. The landscape is modeled as correlated quenched Gaussian random fields.

main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the existence of a homogenized diffusive regime for long-time limits and uses approximations relating $\alpha_2(t)$ to the variance of the time-integrated local mobility.
